question: If an object is manifested by mere arising, how can arising alone explain its clarity?
premises: The opponent holds that an object is manifested by the mere birth of cognition.
The opponent also holds that cognition becomes clear in its object because of arising alone.
Both claims rely on the same momentary arising.
inference: If mere arising is sufficient for manifestation and clarity, the opponent must explain how differences in clarity or timing arise.
plain_english: Then even on that view the object is manifested by mere arising; and if clarity of the object is also due simply to arising, that same fact must explain everything.
